summary_text: We found 112 skills in six places: repo-level skills under .agents/skills, the Platform Agent and Cluster Agent profiles, the a2a persona, one agent plugin, and the upstream google/skills mirror under third_party. None is managed by SSS yet, so there are no stale-against-source findings; every finding here comes from reading the files. We compared every pair: 6,216 pairs in all, 4,656 once skills with the same content are counted once. 3,320 pair scores were already cached; 1,336 were scored this run (15 skills had changed or were new). 27 pairs sit at 2 stars or fewer, 21 of them at 0 or 1 star, and 15 more skill pairs are identical byte for byte. Most of that is by design: the shipped gke-* skills are generated from the upstream mirror plus an overlay, so every mirror/shipped pair is a duplicate on purpose and needs no change. The real work is in the hand-maintained Cluster Agent copies, which have drifted from the Platform copies on facts (conflicts below), in a run of out-of-date commands and defaults inside the mirrored skills, and in two disagreements between unrelated skills. The inventory tool reported 48 broken references; we checked each one and every target exists, either at the repo root or at the Platform Agent profile root where the skill runs, so none is filed. A second, sceptical pass re-read every finding against its quoted evidence and changed 1 of them. 107 findings remain: 23 conflicts, 24 out of date, 34 duplicate groups, 5 out of place, 20 unuseful or padded, 1 with front matter that does not parse. No action was applied and no pull request was opened in this run, at the user's request.

inventory.description: Edit, sync or start mirroring a `gke-*` skill in `agents/platform/skills/` that is copied from google/skills. Use when changing one of those skills, updating it to upstream, or resolving a skill sync conflict.
inventory.goal: Change, sync or adopt a gke-* skill copied from google/skills so the local edit is recorded as an overlay patch and survives the next upstream sync.
inventory.adds: Edit the shipped skill and record it with make skills-refresh (one patch per reason, headers Why/Local-Issue/Retire-When/Upstream-Issue), never touch third_party or upstream.lock by hand, sync only for a concrete reason and in its own PR with the eval loop, and leave stopping a mirror to a maintainer.

inventory.description: Install, set up, or deploy kube-agents (the Kubernetes Agentic Harness) and its Platform Agent onto a GKE cluster in a GCP project, interactively or non-interactively. Use when asked to install, bootstrap, or onboard kube-agents, or to plan one with a dry run.
inventory.goal: Guide an agent through installing kube-agents on a GKE cluster safely: find out what the operator has, agree every choice, preview the install, and apply only after they confirm.
inventory.adds: The team's install protocol: always run `install.sh --non-interactive` in three stages (detect and interview, `--dry-run` preview, explicit go-ahead then apply), read the exit code before the report file, never ask for a secret in chat, never pass an adoption flag (`--migrate-node-pools`, `--enable-network-policy`, `--accept-no-network-policy`, `--enable-gvisor=false`) the operator did not choose, treat `REFUSED_*` as a question not a failure, keep `--permission-set=read-only` unless asked, pin to a release tag rather than `main`, and hand a chat-less install over with the installer's two printed terminal commands verbatim.

inventory.description: Address review feedback on an open pull request: triage and fix findings, reply in every thread, resolve the addressed ones, and request a re-read only while one is owed. Use after an automated or human reviewer reviews a pull request.
inventory.goal: Work a review round on an open pull request: fix or decline each finding, reply in every thread, resolve what was settled, and stop asking for re-reads once the bot is green or a human owns it.
inventory.adds: Decline by default on later rounds (fix only a behaviour Medium on code this PR added by one mechanical edit, fix a correct High on any round, defer anything that adds a mechanism to an issue), keep Self-Review and Live validation current in the same push, at most two self-requested re-reads before green and none after, resolve a declined bot thread only once a human rules.

inventory.description: Reviews a change adversarially — establishes what it claims to do, hunts candidates from ten angles, then re-derives every candidate from source as a hostile second reader and reports only what survives.
inventory.goal: Review a diff range as a hostile second reader: derive its intent, hunt candidates from ten angles, re-verify every candidate against source, and report only confirmed or plausible defects with a disposition.
inventory.adds: Run the pass in a context that did not write the change and withhold intent and commit bodies from it, work all ten named angles with up to six candidates each, verify each candidate to CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/REFUTED and delete the refuted without a trace, edit on CONFIRMED but only report on PLAUSIBLE, and grade with BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW kept separate from the verdict.

inventory.description: Reviews a pull request for documentation drift — finds which docs the change should have updated, verifies doc claims against source, and checks the docs map and AGENTS.md themselves for staleness.
inventory.goal: Check a pull request in both directions for documentation drift: which docs the code change invalidated, and whether changed docs match source, the canonical-home rules and the docs map.
inventory.adds: Navigate only through AGENTS.md's rules and docs/README.md's map, test every doc sentence naming an identifier against the PR's source rather than other docs, treat map churn and maintainer identifiers on site pages as Blocking, derive the map's staleness window from git, and report a Blocking/Advisory triage table instead of fixing silently.

inventory.description: Runs the review passes required before a pull request is opened — adversarial and docs-drift — each in a context that did not write the change, and merges what they return into one disposition list.
inventory.goal: Run the adversarial and docs-drift passes before a pull request opens, each in a fresh context that did not write the change, and merge their results into the Self-Review list.
inventory.adds: Fetch the base into refs/kube-agents-base and diff three-dot before any pass, run make docs-check in the main loop and hand its output on, always spawn both passes concurrently with intent and commit bodies withheld and editing forbidden, block rather than run the pass in the authoring context, keep each pass's own severity vocabulary when merging, and re-run only what a fix invalidated with a fresh context.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes Admission Control (Webhooks, VAP/MAP) for vulnerabilities.
inventory.goal: Review admission webhooks and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy/MutatingAdmissionPolicy objects for bypass, denial-of-service, scope-evasion and unsafe-mutation risks.
inventory.adds: Prefer failurePolicy Fail on security webhooks and VAPs, require a NetworkPolicy limiting webhook ingress to the API server, and ask whether reinvocationPolicy IfNeeded plus a confirming validating webhook is needed for expected mutations.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes and application audit logging for AI agents, ensuring tamper-proof observability.
inventory.goal: Review the logging setup around AI agent workloads so every agent action, prompt and tool call is recorded where the agent cannot alter it.
inventory.adds: Require a dedicated ServiceAccount per agent, stdout/stderr logging with no hostPath access to aggregated logs, full prompt and raw output telemetry plus exact tool input/output logging, and scrubbing of secrets and PII before logs are written.

inventory.description: Reviews AI agent Kubernetes configurations for credentials exposed to agents.
inventory.goal: Review AI agent pod and RBAC configuration so the agent container never holds credentials directly.
inventory.adds: Route all authenticated outbound requests through an injecting credential proxy sidecar, forbid secret env vars and mounts in the agent container, set automountServiceAccountToken false and mount a token only in the sidecar, and flag default ServiceAccounts and RBAC wildcards.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes configurations to prevent data exfiltration by AI agents.
inventory.goal: Review network egress and data-access configuration so a prompt-injected AI agent cannot send data out of the cluster.
inventory.adds: Require egress NetworkPolicies allowlisting only internal services and authorized LLM APIs, route outbound traffic through an egress gateway or transparent proxy with SNI allowlisting, and flag broad RBAC on secrets and configmaps or shared sensitive mounts.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes network and firewall configurations specifically for AI agent execution sandboxes.
inventory.goal: Check the network rules around an AI agent and its execution sandbox so the agent cannot reach things it should not and nothing untrusted can call it.
inventory.adds: Sandbox egress is default-deny with a minimal allowlist, and a metadata-server block must target the credential ports (TCP 80 pre-NAT, 988 post-NAT) and leave port 53 open because under Cloud DNS for GKE the Pod resolver lives at 169.254.169.254:53.

inventory.description: Orchestrates comprehensive Kubernetes security audits specifically tailored for AI agent workloads.
inventory.goal: Run the six AI-agent security review skills in parallel, filter their findings against the project context, and return one JSON report.
inventory.adds: Fan out to the fixed set of six agents-* review skills, require each to answer in the `[{agent, findings:[{message,file,line}]}]` JSON shape, then drop findings the architecture already mitigates (for example root-in-sandbox when a VM-based RuntimeClass is confirmed) before merging.

inventory.description: Reviews AI agent architectures (API gateways, WAFs, input sanitization) for prompt injection risks.
inventory.goal: Check that an AI agent's inputs pass through a filtering layer and that its system prompts cannot be edited by less trusted workloads.
inventory.adds: Nothing

inventory.description: Reviews AI agent execution sandboxes for code escape and lateral movement risks.
inventory.goal: Check that the place where an AI agent runs code (a REPL, shell or WASM tool) is isolated so a hijacked agent cannot break out or persist.
inventory.adds: A sandbox is treated as hostile: it must run under a secure RuntimeClass (gVisor or Kata), be separate from the agent loop container, carry a restrictive seccomp/AppArmor profile, be disposable per run, and have aggressively low CPU, memory and ephemeral-storage limits.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes Gateway API configs (Gateway, HTTPRoute, etc.) for security risks.
inventory.goal: Check Gateway API objects (Gateway, HTTPRoute, TLSRoute, ReferenceGrant) for route takeover, loose cross-namespace access and weak TLS.
inventory.adds: Listeners must restrict `allowedRoutes` to `namespaces.from: Same` or a `Selector`, every cross-namespace route or Secret reference needs a narrow `ReferenceGrant`, and wildcard or broad hostnames are findings unless justified.

inventory.description: Orchestrates comprehensive Kubernetes security reviews.
inventory.goal: Run the whole Kubernetes security review family in parallel, filter the findings against the project context, and return one JSON report.
inventory.adds: First call review-security-k8s-understand, then fan out to the fixed list of ten review skills (including the agents orchestrator), require the shared `[{agent, findings:[{message,file,line}]}]` JSON shape, and drop findings a recognised infrastructure role or a confirmed service mesh already mitigates before merging.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes namespace configurations for workload isolation, multi-tenancy, and boundary defense.
inventory.goal: Check how a cluster is split into namespaces so tenants and environments stay apart and nobody hides workloads in system namespaces.
inventory.adds: Flag when more than roughly 80-90% of workloads share one namespace, any custom workload in `default`/`kube-*`, namespace names that imitate system components, policy-bypass labels such as `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged`, and Secrets, ServiceAccounts or RoleBindings left in namespaces with no running pods.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes network configurations (NetworkPolicies, Services, Ingress) for isolation and exposure risks.
inventory.goal: Check NetworkPolicies, Services, Ingresses and service-mesh policies so workloads are isolated and nothing is exposed by accident.
inventory.adds: Every namespace needs a default-deny NetworkPolicy for both ingress and egress, any `NodePort` or `hostNetwork: true` is a finding, Ingresses need a `tls` block plus HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, exposed ports 22/3389/2379/10250 and hand-written `Endpoints`/`EndpointSlice` are flagged, and a mesh must enforce `STRICT` mTLS with default-deny AuthorizationPolicies.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes manifests for node boundary violations and risks of node-to-cluster privilege escalation.
inventory.goal: Check manifests for ways a pod or a compromised node could take over the rest of the cluster through host mounts, node RBAC or scheduling.
inventory.adds: Flag hostPath mounts to kubelet or control-plane directories and runtime sockets and recommend ValidatingAdmissionPolicies as the fix, flag any extra RBAC on `system:nodes` (bindings, `impersonate`, write verbs on `nodes`/`nodes/status`), and flag key-less `operator: Exists` tolerations on untrusted workloads.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes Pod security contexts for workload-level isolation and privilege escalation risks.
inventory.goal: Give a reviewer a fixed checklist for judging whether a Pod's security context lets it escape or escalate.
inventory.adds: The team's pod baseline is the restricted Pod Security Standard plus three extras: images pinned by digest, no `default` service account or static token Secrets, and an omitted `hostUsers` is flagged whenever the pod runs as UID/GID 0.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes RBAC configurations for permissions and privilege escalation risks.
inventory.goal: Give a reviewer a fixed checklist for finding over-broad or escalatable RBAC roles and bindings, tuned to GKE.
inventory.adds: RBAC review is graded against the GKE RBAC best-practices checklist (default groups, wildcards, CSR/webhook/CRD write verbs, secrets list/watch, self-modification) and the reviewer must also report any item from that checklist the skill's own list omits.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes ServiceAccount configurations for identity management and least privilege boundaries.
inventory.goal: Give a reviewer a fixed checklist for ServiceAccount identity hygiene: one account per app, no automount, no long-lived tokens.
inventory.adds: The team requires a 1:1 application-to-ServiceAccount mapping (including one Workload Identity cloud identity per workload), `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the ServiceAccount object itself, and flags ServiceAccounts that hold bindings but run no workload.

inventory.description: Reviews Kubernetes storage configurations, PVs, and VolumeMounts for data leakage and privilege escalation risks.
inventory.goal: Give a reviewer a fixed checklist for storage objects and volume mounts that could leak data or let a container reach the node.
inventory.adds: The team's storage defaults are: mounts read-only unless write is needed, `ReadWriteMany` flagged in favour of RWO/ROX, encryption at rest (CMEK) required on StorageClasses, `Retain` flagged on sensitive volumes without a wipe process, and `allowVolumeExpansion` flagged unless a ResourceQuota bounds it.

inventory.description: Analyzes Kubernetes project architecture and resources to build context before performing specific security reviews.
inventory.goal: Build a short architectural picture of a Kubernetes repo before the specialised security review skills run on it.
inventory.adds: Before any specialised review, the reviewer must classify every workload as Infrastructure or Application and list cluster-wide compensating controls (mesh mTLS, Gatekeeper policies) in one concise summary that the later reviews read first.

inventory.description: Reviews agent skill definitions for token efficiency, clarity, and standardized formatting.
inventory.goal: Review a SKILL.md against this repo's house style so it is short, loadable, and found by the harness when a user asks for it.
inventory.adds: House style for skills: the frontmatter description opens with the action the user asks for and names the object (the harness matches on it), frontmatter must parse as YAML, the body uses `# Task` plus `# Checks`/`# Workflow` with terse headers, bullets start with `Flag`/`Require`/`Ensure`, no persona preambles, and no check or domain fact is dropped while shortening.

inventory.description: Uninstall kube-agents (the Kubernetes Agentic Harness) — discover and remove the GCP/GKE infrastructure an install provisioned. Use when asked to uninstall, remove, or tear down kube-agents from a project or cluster.
inventory.goal: Remove a kube-agents install and the GCP/GKE resources it provisioned using the project's own uninstall script.
inventory.adds: Run the uninstall.sh pinned to the installed release (or pass --source-ref) rather than an unstamped copy that falls back to main, with terraform (and helm on a non-created cluster) on PATH, treat exit 3 as nothing-to-tear-down and not a failure, and on a kept cluster after a GitLab install tell the operator the token and CA Secrets stay and that the token must be revoked in GitLab.

inventory.description: Upgrade kube-agents (the Kubernetes Agentic Harness) and its operator on a GKE cluster, interactively or non-interactively. Use when asked to upgrade, update, or apply a Day-2 change to an existing kube-agents install.
inventory.goal: Guide an agent through upgrading a running kube-agents install to a chosen release with the correct upgrade.sh flags and mode.
inventory.adds: Upgrade only through the release-pinned upgrade.sh (or a bundle's own copy) with full mode as the default, pass --image-tag only for a CI/dev candidate (SemVer tag or full SHA, never a mutable ref), use --plan rather than --dry-run when drift against real Terraform state matters, and give every run the install's install.env (via KUBE_AGENTS_INSTALL_ENV on an ephemeral runner).

inventory.description: Read and write the agent blackboard - the durable, named topics on the A2A bus where agents publish what they currently know (upgrade readiness, the environment blueprint, dated annotations). Use when asked about fleet or environment state that another agent may already have assessed, before starting a fresh diagnosis, and to record a finding other agents should start from. Do not use for task status (that is stream replay, not a topic), for anything not in `a2a topics list`, or on an install where the A2A bus is not running.
inventory.goal: Let an agent read and publish standing fleet state on named A2A bus topics instead of re-diagnosing what another agent already found.
inventory.adds: Before a fresh diagnosis check `a2a topics list`/`read`; relay the entry's author and date verbatim and never present it as your own check; treat exit 2 as 'provisioned but unwritten'; write only topics this profile owns, with `--text` plus `--data` and the task/context/correlation ids when you have them; put dated findings in `annotations` one per finding; and when `NATS_URL` or the `a2a` binary is absent, say the bus is unreachable rather than working around the sandbox.

inventory.description: Act upon GKE cluster-autoscaler stockout alerts, diagnose them using ComputeClass debugging guidelines, and submit a remediation Pull Request.
inventory.goal: Turn a GKE autoscaler stockout alert from Pub/Sub into a diagnosed root cause and a GitOps pull request that adds ComputeClass fallbacks or fixes the workload shape.
inventory.adds: A fixed runbook: notify via `send_notification` first, never use `execute_code` in Pub/Sub sessions, dedupe only by the fixed branch `platform-agent/remediate-stockout-<workload>` through `vcs.py proposal list --source`, stop on a false signal (no Pending pods), take the working copy with `submit_suggestion.py prepare`, run the mandated quota/reservation/Spot-advice/autoscaler-status checks, apply the eight ComputeClass rules (fallbacks, >32 vCPU shapes, disk-generation mix, on-demand floor, regional scarcity with a migration playbook, quota cap, >10 granular machineType rules compressed to four families, Hyperdisk-incompatible fallbacks), annotate every YAML change with `# Remediation:`, stage files by path, and open the PR with `submit_suggestion.py submit --body-file` carrying a literal `Checks Performed` block.

inventory.description: Workflows for setting up and auditing observability (logging, monitoring, tracing) on GKE.
inventory.goal: Help the per-cluster agent check whether a GKE cluster's logging, metrics and tracing are set up and report what to turn on.
inventory.adds: The Cluster Agent never runs an observability change; it reports each one as a proposal expressed as a Config Connector ContainerCluster field (managedPrometheus.enabled, monitoringConfig.enableComponents with APISERVER/SCHEDULER/CONTROLLER_MANAGER, advancedDatapathObservabilityConfig) for the Platform Agent to apply.

inventory.description: Workflows for ensuring high availability and reliability of GKE workloads.
inventory.goal: Check a single GKE cluster and its workloads for availability gaps (regional control plane, PDBs, probes, graceful shutdown, zone spread, maintenance windows) and propose, not apply, the fixes.
inventory.adds: The agent runs this as a read-only audit whose output is proposals in the report (never applied changes), it treats regional control plane, a readiness probe on every production container, a PDB on critical apps and zone topology spread as mandatory for production, and it expresses a proposed maintenance window as a Config Connector ContainerCluster spec.maintenancePolicy.recurringWindow with FREQ=DAILY rather than a gcloud command.

inventory.description: Read-only detection of controllers that stopped making progress without erroring — observedGeneration lag, stuck progress conditions, repeating warning events, and references to objects that do not exist — in one namespace or one kind.
inventory.goal: Find controllers that silently stopped reconciling (no error, no progress) in one namespace or kind, using a read-only report script.
inventory.adds: Stall detection is the four heuristics in `/opt/data/scripts/stall_report.py` (generation-lag, stale-condition, repeating-warnings, dangling-reference) gated by a 15-minute default horizon (10 for Deployments), run against the namespace that owns the stalled object; the Cluster Agent reports via `kanban_complete` (or the card's own template), quotes the `stalled resources: <count>` line, notes that Secret references go unchecked under the default read-only identity, and proposes patches without applying them.

inventory.description: Guidance on managing storage in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters.
inventory.goal: Tells the Cluster Agent how GKE storage is set up: StorageClasses, the CSI drivers, and growing a PVC.
inventory.adds: Nothing

inventory.description: Specific workflows for scaling GKE workloads using HPA and VPA, as well as best practices for autoscaling configuration.
inventory.goal: Help the Cluster Agent recommend how a GKE workload should be scaled, by hand or with HPA and VPA, without applying anything itself.
inventory.adds: Scaling changes are reported as proposals (a Deployment replicas patch, HPA/VPA manifests, or Config Connector ContainerCluster/ContainerNodePool fields), never executed, and the house pattern is HPA on CPU with VPA on memory.

inventory.description: Workflows for auditing and hardening the security of GKE workloads.
inventory.goal: Help the per-cluster agent check how well a GKE cluster's workloads are secured and write up the fixes it would make.
inventory.adds: Because the Cluster Agent is read-only, every hardening step is reported as a proposal expressed as a Kubernetes manifest or Config Connector field rather than a kubectl/gcloud command, and Calico enablement on non-DPv2 clusters is proposed only after checking the dataplane, as two ordered changes (control-plane addon first, then node enforcement).

inventory.description: Systematic Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for diagnosing GKE workload failures, crash loops, resource OOMs, mounting errors, and connectivity timeouts.
inventory.goal: The step-by-step procedure the Cluster Agent follows to diagnose a failing GKE workload and hand the root cause and a patch back on its kanban card.
inventory.adds: Diagnose in a fixed order (pod status, namespace events, logs, connectivity) inside a one-hour window centred on the container's last state transition, use git history to find the last good image tag, query `mcp-developer_knowledge` before web search, and finish by calling `kanban_complete` with the whole RCA in `result` (aim under 2,000 characters) and the patch in `metadata`, never applying to the cluster, opening a PR, or putting the RCA in the chat reply.

inventory.description: Check GKE quota and live hardware obtainability before recommending capacity, and plan future capacity windows for deadline-bound batch jobs. Use when a cluster design, capacity plan, scale-up decision, GPU/TPU batch schedule, or a free-standing availability question needs live evidence: regional quota verification (gcloud compute regions describe), reservations, capacity obtainability advice (gcloud beta compute advice capacity / capacity-history) across zones and provisioning models, and future window advice (gcloud beta compute advice calendar-mode) for "when will this shape be obtainable". For handling an inbound cluster-autoscaler stockout alert end to end — triage, GitOps remediation, Pull Request — use the gke-stockout-investigator plugin skill instead.
inventory.goal: Gather live quota and hardware-availability evidence before recommending GKE capacity, and find future reservation windows for deadline-bound GPU/TPU batch jobs.
inventory.adds: Report quota and live obtainability separately with the verbatim sentence "Quota is separate from live capacity." and never the word "guarantee", probe Spot and Flex-Start across at least two zones and name all three provisioning paths, record every check with `record_evidence` and every manifest with `attach_artifact` in the pinned JSON shapes (chips not nodes, one-day reservation floor, start range computed at probe time), rank calendar-mode windows earliest-first with quota headroom as tiebreak, and check ComputeClass designs against resilience rules A to H (On-Demand floor, no Gen 2/Gen 4 PV mix, at most family-level priorities, Hyperdisk-compatible fallbacks).

inventory.description: Create, delegate to, and tear down per-cluster Cluster Agent Hermes profiles. Use whenever a GKE cluster is onboarded, deleted or taken out of management, or whenever a single-cluster runtime debugging/operations task should be delegated to that cluster's Cluster Agent.
inventory.goal: Tells the Platform Agent when to create or delete a cluster's Cluster Agent profile and how to hand single-cluster debugging work to it through the kanban board.
inventory.adds: Profiles are created only at onboarding and deleted only at teardown (never repaired from other work or by the discovery sweep; use scope exclusion for a live cluster), single-cluster runtime debugging is always delegated via a kanban card assigned to an `exists` profile (fan-out: one parentless card per cluster, poll, then synthesize before completing your own card), and the read-only Cluster Agent never opens PRs so the Platform Agent does via `submit-suggestion` only when the request asked for a change.

inventory.description: Publish the findings of an autonomous fleet audit as one continuously-rewritten issue per audit stream on the GitOps repository's forge, and propose fixes as narrow remediation pull requests (merge requests on GitLab).
inventory.goal: Lets the Platform Agent run a fleet audit and publish what it found as one tracked ledger issue per audit stream plus small fix pull requests, with the harness script doing every forge write.
inventory.adds: The agent only inspects read-only and emits a validated findings.json (one finding per durable object, literal commands per check, no invented ids, timestamps or bodies), while audit_report.py owns every git/forge action, id derivation, ledger rewrite, delta, the five-per-run critical auto-promotion, partial/held/clean semantics and the `silent_ok` verdict; never re-enact a cron job inline, never pad `checks_run`, and never open a second ledger or a PR by hand.

inventory.description: Answer a question about a past autonomous fleet audit from the on-pod report store — what a stream last found, how many criticals are open, what changed between two runs, which clusters were skipped or only partly covered, and when each stream last ran. Never the answer to a request to run an audit: a run collects, publishes and opens its fixes through the fleet-audit skill.
inventory.goal: Answer questions about what earlier fleet audits found by querying the stored run envelopes through a small script instead of reading the large report files.
inventory.adds: Answer every question about a past audit only through report_query.py's seven bounded subcommands, never by opening a store file; treat an absent, unreadable, never-run or died stream as unknown rather than clean; quote only counts and ids the script returned (e.g. added_total, not len(added)); caveat deltas when partial, ledger_held_open or delta_known=false is set; always hand back the issue URL except on NO_FORGE; and never run, publish, remediate or act on a lease from this skill because fleet-audit owns that lifecycle.

inventory.description: Reports every GKE cluster's control-plane and node-pool versions against a target version or each cluster's release-channel default, naming the members that lag and by how many minors; run again during a rollout, it shows which members started, completed or stalled since the previous run; with --readiness, it also grades each member on what would stop the upgrade, naming drain-blocking PodDisruptionBudgets, fail-closed admission webhooks in the upgrade's path or able to refuse the control plane's bootstrap RBAC writes (ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings; Roles and RoleBindings in kube-system and kube-public) with an unreachable backend, maintenance exclusions and windows, and node-pool version skew. Scans the linked GitOps repositories' manifests for apiVersions the target removes, with each hit's replacement. Read-only against GCP, the clusters and Git, from gcloud container, kubectl get and repository reads, keeping only its own record of each run and per-member kubeconfig files; the executed counterpart to gke-upgrades' advice.
inventory.goal: Tell an operator which GKE clusters in the fleet lag a target version, what would stop their upgrade, and which GitOps manifests that version would break.
inventory.adds: Fleet version, rollout and readiness questions are answered by one run of the skill's scripts from the Platform profile (never a per-cluster fan-out or a hand kubectl/gcloud survey); the agent reports the table's grades verbatim without re-grading, keeps patch-behind apart from lagging, treats a stall as an observation not a fault, names an exclusion as holding back automatic upgrades only, recommends but never runs the upgrade or the manifest migrations, and cites no CVE identifiers.

inventory.description: Audits standalone GCE virtual machines, Managed Instance Groups (MIGs), serial console boot failures, sole-tenant node group headroom, and orphaned disk snapshots.
inventory.goal: Run the GCE collector for standalone VMs, MIGs, sole-tenant node groups and orphaned snapshots, and hand its findings to the fleet-audit harness.
inventory.adds: Open the run with fleet-audit `start` before anything else, pass the `fleet_scope` tool's `collector_args` to the collector verbatim, treat all four roster checks as collector-verified and never hand-run them, keep `ops-agent-guest-health` off the roster, and `finish` with `--manifest-file` so `checks_run` is cross-checked against what ran.

inventory.description: Authors Config Connector (KCC) manifests for Google Cloud resource changes and hands them to submit-suggestion as a pull request under the GitOps repository's clusters/<cluster>/provisioning/ path. Use when a request changes a GKE cluster or node pool (grow, autoscale, adopt), a Cloud SQL instance (add a read replica, resize), or a VPC firewall rule on an install whose GitOps repository holds Config Connector YAML. Decides create versus acquire read-only, validates every field with kubectl explain against the customer's CRDs, and never applies. Don't use for Kubernetes workload manifests (use gke-manifest-generation), imperative cluster creation (use gke-cluster-creation), or Terraform HCL.
inventory.goal: Write Config Connector manifests for GKE node pool, Cloud SQL and VPC firewall changes and submit them as a GitOps pull request without applying anything.
inventory.adds: Check the CRD first, open the repo with submit-suggestion `prepare` on branch `platform-agent/kcc-<kind>-<name>`, decide create/acquire/edit from the read-only decision table before writing, put `deletion-policy: abandon` and `state-into-spec: absent` on every manifest, state only required fields, identifying immutable fields and the requested change, validate each spec path with `kubectl explain` instead of a server dry-run, stop for the user on any immutable-field change, and use the fixed PR-body section.

inventory.description: Audits VPC subnet IPAM capacity, Cloud NAT port exhaustion, Private Service Connect routing, VPC peering MTU mismatches, Cloud Armor WAF policies, and management ports open to the whole internet.

inventory.description: Read and analyze the source of any repository on GitHub or on another forge this install serves (GitLab) — public or one this install has a token for — without a local checkout. Clones broker-side and pulls file content back; use it to answer questions about code, not to change it.
inventory.goal: Let the Platform Agent read the source of a repository it has no checkout of, by having the credential broker clone it and pass file content back.
inventory.adds: Reads of foreign repositories go through the broker's read-only workspace (clone for small trees, open/grep/fetch/close for large ones) with --depth 1, fetching only paths that list or grep returned, treating truncated/stopped/skipped as part of the answer, never running git on what lands, and reporting owner/name@sha.

inventory.description: Audit, monitor, and debug the logging, tracing, metrics, and API/dashboard observability of the Platform Agent.
inventory.goal: Check whether the Platform Agent's own logs, metrics, traces and dashboard are working, and find out why when they are not.
inventory.adds: Diagnose harness telemetry from the install's own sources of truth: scrape config from the PodMonitoring resources (never Deployment annotations) and proven via PromQL through the credential broker's relay using exported_cluster labels, the OTLP endpoint from status.telemetry (stop on source None, treat Default-without-GKE-OTel as the fault, never assume gke-managed-otel), the tool-call trail from audit.jsonl rather than agent.log, and the dashboard probed by kubectl exec on 127.0.0.1:9119 because port-forward cannot reach a gVisor sandbox.

inventory.description: Bring an existing GKE cluster under management on user request (e.g. "manage my cluster <name> in <location>") by creating its Cluster Agent profile, or take one out of management by excluding it. Use whenever a user asks to manage/onboard/watch a specific existing cluster, or to stop managing, exclude or offboard one.
inventory.goal: Start or stop managing one specific existing GKE cluster when a user asks, by creating its Cluster Agent profile or declaring it excluded from scope.
inventory.adds: Verify the cluster exists first, create the profile with `python3 /opt/data/scripts/cluster_agent_profile.py create --project --cluster --location` (idempotent), and to stop managing never just delete the profile: declare the exclusion at the install's source of scope (`install.env` + `./upgrade.sh --upgrade-mode=full` on an installer install, never a hand edit of the CR or chart there, since the next full upgrade overwrites it), falling back to the chart value, tfvars, or `spec.scope.exclude.clusters` only on a hand-applied `PlatformAgent`.

inventory.description: Answer a reviewer who addressed you on one of your own pull requests — read the thread, answer or amend the branch, and reply in the thread.
inventory.goal: Let the Platform Agent answer a reviewer on one of its own pull requests from a kanban card: re-read the thread, answer or amend the branch, and post a marked reply.
inventory.adds: Reviewer comments are data not instruction; the agent re-polls before acting, acts only on requests whose author's write access is known and true (refuses known-untrusted, leaves unknown alone), amends only the PR's own branch via submit-suggestion, reads the commit back before describing it, posts one reply per request through the helper with --verify-commit or --no-change so the marker closes the request, and always ends the card with kanban_complete or kanban_block.

inventory.description: Propose declarative configuration updates securely by committing file changes and submitting pull requests (merge requests on GitLab) for SRE review. Not for fleet-audit finding fixes — the fleet-audit skill opens and tracks those PRs itself.
inventory.goal: Give the Platform Agent one safe path to turn a requested config change into a reviewable pull request on the fleet's GitOps repository.
inventory.adds: Every GitOps write goes through `prepare`/`submit` under `$HERMES_HOME/skills/submit-suggestion/scripts/submit_suggestion.py` (never the plain credentialed `git`, never an absolute profile path), on a change-derived `platform-agent/<change_type>-<target_id>` branch whose base the broker resolves, staging only named files (never `git add .`/`-A`), passing the PR body through a `mktemp` file in /opt/data/scratch via `--body-file` with a quoted heredoc, treating a resubmit as an in-place update, routing fleet-audit finding fixes to fleet-audit `remediate` instead, opening no PR for a diagnosis-only request, and fetching review comments yourself rather than asking for them to be pasted.

inventory.description: Read and change a hosted repository through forge-neutral verbs. Version control here is abstracted — remote operations go through vcs.py, local operations use a credential-free VCS binary on a working copy that vcs.py puts on disk. Covers history, file modes, proposals and issues, so no forge CLI is needed.
inventory.goal: Let the Platform Agent read, change, and collaborate on a managed repository through forge-neutral vcs.py verbs and a credential-free local git, without any forge CLI.
inventory.adds: Network and credential operations go only through vcs.py's broker verbs (clone as bundle, publish, proposal/issue/label/identity/remote-branch) and never through gh, git push/fetch/clone or a hand-built URL; local git is for reading and committing in the cloned copy; branch before committing, name the paths you commit, obey the refusal codes (NOT_FAST_FORWARD, BASE_MOVED, TARGET_NOT_BASE, BRANCH_NOT_OURS...) rather than forcing, discard when done, and treat commentsTruncated as a reason not to answer.

inventory.description: Orchestrate cross-cluster workload rebalancing using the kanban board with the validation-then-declare pattern. Use when fleet utilization shows one cluster overutilized and another with headroom and a workload should move.
inventory.goal: Let the Platform Agent move a workload from an overloaded cluster to one with headroom by fanning out read-only validation cards to cluster agents and then declaring the move as a single GitOps PR.
inventory.adds: Validation-then-declare: resolve each cluster's profile with get_cluster_profile_name, open two parent-less kanban cards (can-host on the target, safe-to-evacuate on the source) with the given metadata contracts, poll them with kanban_show, and only when both are green open one PR via submit-suggestion and record the decision in kanban_complete metadata; any red means no declaration and needs_input escalation; agents never mutate clusters.

inventory.description: Diagnoses, predicts, and mitigates node disruptions during Compute Engine host maintenance and hardware or software maintenance events for GPU and TPU workloads on GKE. Use when diagnosing node disruptions, predicting host maintenance events on GPU/TPU nodepools, inspecting node interruption PromQL metrics, auditing node taints, or configuring workload protection strategies (graceful termination, opportunistic maintenance, PodDisruptionBudgets). Don't use for general GKE cluster creation, network policy configuration, or non-disruption workload deployment.
inventory.goal: Decide whether a GPU or TPU node disruption came from Compute Engine host maintenance and recommend protections for the workload.
inventory.adds: Halt and ask for project, location, cluster and timestamp before offering theories; always present the `kubernetes_io:node_interruption_count` PromQL filtered on `HW/SW Maintenance`; when labels, metrics and logs are all empty state that host maintenance is ruled out and point to application causes; never recommend tolerating the impending-termination taint; and recommend graceful termination, opportunistic maintenance and PodDisruptionBudgets together.

inventory.description: Diagnoses GKE JobSet interruptions, restarts, and preemptions for AI/ML training workloads autonomously. Use when troubleshooting JobSet restart loops, spot VM preemptions, node readiness failures, host VM issues, or coordinator worker crashes. Don't use for general GKE cluster creation, basic workload deployment, or non-JobSet application issues.
inventory.goal: Diagnose why a GKE JobSet keeps restarting (Spot preemption, host failure, worker crash) and recommend a scheduling or host-quarantine fix.
inventory.adds: Work the four steps in a fixed order (JobSet restarts, nodepool interruptions, node-to-host correlation, pod phases then worker logs) using the paired MQL, PromQL and LQL templates inside a plus-or-minus 30 minute window, do not enter credential-troubleshooting loops on a 403 but complete the workflow from templates and staged telemetry, and recommend On-Demand or compact placement for preemptions and cordon-drain-recreate plus a support ticket for a repeat-failing host.

inventory.description: Diagnoses and prevents vbar_control_agent segfaults, out-of-memory (OOM) errors, and TPU device initialization failures on TPU v6e nodes in GKE caused by race conditions during TPU device resets or high-frequency metrics polling. Use when troubleshooting vbar_control_agent crashes, memory cgroup OOMs in serial console logs, tpu-device-plugin metrics checksum corruption errors, or custom TPU metrics collection conflicts on GKE TPU v6e nodes. Don't use for general non-TPU container OOM troubleshooting or standard GKE node lifecycle operations.
inventory.goal: Walk an agent through diagnosing vbar_control_agent OOMs and TPU device-plugin checksum errors on GKE TPU v6e nodes, and advising on the fix.
inventory.adds: Diagnose TPU v6e vbar_control_agent crashes in a fixed order inside a +/-30-minute window (serial-console OOM, tpu-device-plugin checksum errors, then search for custom libtpu.sdk.tpumonitoring collectors), answer informational requests with the filter templates instead of running them, and recommend disabling the custom collector until the GKE-side fix ships.

inventory.description: Manages GKE application onboarding, covering containerization, deployment manifests, and migration. Use when onboarding or deploying an application to GKE for the first time, or containerizing an app for GKE. Don't use for general GKE cluster administration or upgrades (use gke-basics or gke-upgrades instead).
inventory.goal: Guide an agent through containerizing an application and deploying it to GKE for the first time: assess, build the image, push to Artifact Registry, write manifests, apply them.
inventory.adds: Prefer multi-stage distroless non-root images (or Buildpacks when no Dockerfile is wanted), push to Artifact Registry with vulnerability scanning on, ship manifests with requests/limits, liveness and readiness probes, at least two replicas and ClusterIP plus Gateway API for external traffic, and apply through the GKE MCP apply_k8s_manifest before falling back to kubectl.

inventory.description: Configures Backup for GKE: the BackupRestore cluster addon, BackupPlan and RestorePlan resources, restore workflows, and CMEK-encrypted backups. Use for backup policies, disaster recovery, or GKE cluster restores. Don't use for database backups.
inventory.goal: Guide an agent through setting up Backup for GKE (addon, backup plans, restore plans, restores) and running a restore safely.
inventory.adds: Always pass --include-volume-data and --include-secrets explicitly, prefer the safe conflict policies (use-existing-version plus fail-on-conflict), validate restores in a non-production cluster and get explicit user confirmation before a production restore, scope plans to namespaces, enable CMEK and a defined retention as the golden path, call the service 'Backup for GKE', and do not block waiting for the addon enablement to finish.

inventory.description: Manages core GKE cluster provisioning, credentials, Autopilot vs Standard selection, and workload deployment. Use when creating GKE clusters, fetching kubectl credentials, or deciding between Autopilot and Standard modes. Don't use for Workload Identity (use gke-workload-identity), GKE networking (use gke-networking), security hardening (use gke-platform-security or gke-workload-security), or cluster upgrades (use gke-upgrades).
inventory.goal: Give an agent the core rules for creating GKE clusters, fetching credentials and choosing Autopilot versus Standard, plus a tool-preference order and command references.
inventory.adds: Default to Autopilot and justify Standard only by citing the specific restrictions, route to sibling skills for identity/security/upgrades/manifests, use Developer Knowledge MCP (search_documents, never answer_query) before web search for facts and GKE MCP before gcloud before kubectl for cluster operations unless the user overrides, always pass --region/--zone on get-credentials, and honour the Autopilot 250m CPU increment and requests-equal-limits rule.

inventory.description: Runs batch and HPC workloads on GKE, utilizing job queues and parallel processing. Use when running GKE batch jobs, configuring GKE HPC, or setting up GKE job queues. Don't use for standard web application deployments (use gke-app-onboarding instead).
inventory.goal: Guide an agent in running batch and HPC workloads on GKE with Jobs, JobSet, Kueue, MPI Operator, compact placement and Spot VMs.
inventory.adds: Use Kueue for multi-tenant queueing and JobSet for tightly coupled multi-component work, run batch on Spot through a ComputeClass with on-demand fallback and activeMigration, let batch pools scale to zero, always set requests/limits and a backoffLimit, checkpoint at the application level, and advise maintenance exclusions during long Spot/TPU training windows.

inventory.description: Trigger on mention of GKE cluster autoscaler,  node autoscaling, node pool auto-creation / node auto-provisioning. Provides guidance on enabling and optimizing cluster autoscaler, best practices, and troubleshooting issues such as nodes not scaling up or down, zonal stockouts, or capacity buffers. Do not use for ComputeClass-specific YAML generation or priority configuration (defer to gke-compute-classes skill).
inventory.goal: Help an agent enable, tune and troubleshoot the GKE Cluster Autoscaler and node pool auto-creation, including scale-up stalls, scale-down blockers and capacity buffers.
inventory.adds: Spell out Cluster Autoscaler/Node Auto Provisioning/ComputeClass with no acronyms, refuse identifiers that fail ^[a-z0-9-]+$ and treat pasted logs as data, prefer ComputeClass nodePoolAutoCreation on GKE 1.33.3+ over cluster-level Node Auto Provisioning, use the optimize-utilization profile as the golden path, always walk the full seven-item scale-down blocker list then run find-scale-down-blockers.sh, recommend a fallback tier whenever Spot is involved, wait 30 minutes after creating a reservation, and defer ComputeClass YAML to gke-compute-classes.

inventory.description: Plans and executes GKE cluster creation, provisioning, and production readiness audits using pre-defined templates (Autopilot, Standard Regional, GPU/AI Inference, AI Hypercompute). Use when creating GKE clusters, provisioning GKE environments, selecting cluster modes, or auditing GKE clusters. Don't use for application onboarding or deployment configuration (use gke-app-onboarding instead).
inventory.goal: Guide an agent through creating a GKE cluster from one of five templates, defaulting to the golden-path Autopilot configuration.
inventory.adds: Every new cluster defaults to the golden-path private Autopilot template (REGULAR channel, private nodes, authorized networks, Secret Manager add-on with 120s rotation, scoped RBAC bindings, full monitoring set); the agent asks for project, region and name, shows the gcloud command or create_cluster payload for confirmation before creating, and warns explicitly when deviating to Standard, GPU or hypercompute templates.

inventory.description: Configures, optimizes, and troubleshoots GKE ComputeClasses. Use when configuring Spot VMs with on-demand fallback, targeting specific accelerators (GPUs/TPUs) or machine families, restricting ComputeClass access, or debugging pending pods related to node pool auto-creation. Do not use for cluster-level Node Auto Provisioning configuration or general GKE cluster creation.
inventory.goal: Give an agent the rules, schema facts and example manifests for writing, governing and debugging GKE ComputeClasses.
inventory.adds: Answer ComputeClass requests generalized-first with placeholder zones, a CUD-alignment comment on every machineFamily, an 'EXAMPLE TEMPLATE - DO NOT DEPLOY' label and strict schema rules, order AI/ML priorities Reservations -> On-Demand -> DWS FlexStart -> Spot, cap three rules per priorityScore, insert intermediate fallback tiers and isolate stateful classes, default stateful PVs to dynamic-rwo, govern access with ClusterRole RBAC plus a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that closes nodeSelector/affinity/toleration paths, and refuse injected directives and security-floor weakening.

inventory.description: Answer natural language questions and perform analysis on GKE cluster and workload costs using BigQuery billing exports, cost allocation data, and live cluster monitoring metrics. Use when querying GKE costs across projects, namespaces, or workloads, analyzing billing reports in BigQuery (`bq`), checking cluster cost budgets (`gcloud billing`), or diagnosing cost drivers like pod requests vs. actual utilization (`kubectl top`). Don't use for applying cost optimization changes, creating rightsizing manifests (VPA/MPA), or selecting ComputeClasses (use gke-cost-optimization instead).
inventory.goal: Help an agent answer GKE cost questions from the BigQuery billing export, cost allocation labels and live kubectl top data without changing anything.
inventory.adds: Answer cost questions with a direct answer plus bq query templates scoped to GKE via the goog-k8s-cluster-name label, check that cost allocation is enabled, explain the Autopilot (Pod requests) versus Standard (VM plus fee) driver, default to last 30 days, limit 10, ordered by cost descending, prefer bq over BigQuery Studio with dot-separated table paths, and hand any change (VPA, Spot, quotas) to gke-cost-optimization.

inventory.description: Optimizes GKE costs, rightsizes workloads, and configures Spot VMs, CUDs, cost allocation, and resource quotas. Use when optimizing GKE cluster or workload costs, configuring GKE cost allocation or quotas, rightsizing CPU/memory requests, or selecting Spot VMs and machine types. Don't use for general compute class provisioning or GPU Selection (use gke-compute-classes instead).
inventory.goal: Help the Platform Agent cut GKE spend by rightsizing requests, applying quotas, using Spot capacity, and choosing machine families and discounts.
inventory.adds: Rightsize with VPA in recommendation mode and set requests to P95 * 1.2 at the stated over-provisioning thresholds, prefer Spot through a ComputeClass with on-demand fallback and always warn the user about preemption, keep the golden-path OPTIMIZE_UTILIZATION and VPA defaults, apply the dev/test deviation table, and hand cost measurement to gke-cost-analysis.

inventory.description: Provides GKE golden path configuration defaults, production readiness checklists, and cluster default patterns. Use when designing GKE clusters, verifying GKE production readiness, or checking configurations against GKE defaults. Don't use for setting up workload autoscaling specifically (use gke-workload-scaling instead).
inventory.goal: Define the default Autopilot cluster configuration the agent applies, and audits against, when it designs or reviews a production GKE cluster.
inventory.adds: Default every cluster design to the listed Autopilot golden-path values (private nodes, Dataplane V2, Cloud DNS, Secret Manager with 120s rotation, OPTIMIZE_UTILIZATION, the full monitoring component set), prefer MCP over gcloud over kubectl, flag Day-0 decisions and ask before changing a customer-configurable setting, and report audits as deviations with severity and remediation.

inventory.description: Deploys and optimizes AI/ML inference workloads on GKE, using GPUs, TPUs, and model servers. Use when deploying GKE inference servers, configuring GKE GPU resources for inference, or deploying LLMs on GKE. Don't use for generic batch jobs or HPC task queues (use gke-batch-hpc instead).
inventory.goal: Deploy and tune LLM and other AI model servers on GKE with GPUs or TPUs.
inventory.adds: Start from GKE Inference Quickstart (`gcloud container ai profiles`) to pick the model, server and accelerator tuple and generate the manifest, run it on an Autopilot cluster through a GPU ComputeClass, and autoscale on DCGM GPU metrics with long scale-down windows.

inventory.description: Generates and updates secure, production-ready Kubernetes YAML manifests optimized for GKE Autopilot and GKE Standard clusters. Use when creating or modifying GKE deployment manifests, configuring container security contexts, setting CPU/memory resource limits, defining readiness/liveness/startup probes, mounting secrets and volumes, configuring GKE Gateway API routes, targeting Spot VMs, or deploying AI model inference workloads (vLLM, TGI, Gemma). Don't use for live cluster operations, pod troubleshooting (use gke-workload-troubleshooting), or cluster infrastructure provisioning (use gke-cluster-creation).
inventory.goal: Generate or edit Kubernetes manifests for GKE workloads that follow a fixed set of security, sizing, probe and routing rules.
inventory.adds: House defaults for every manifest: explicit namespace and a dedicated ServiceAccount, conservative Standard requests with 2x-4x limits and equal requests/limits on Autopilot, Spot VM nodeSelector plus toleration for -dev/-test/-staging namespaces, non-root/read-only/seccomp security contexts with secrets mounted as 0400 files, mandatory liveness and readiness probes plus a startupProbe for slow starters, ClusterIP with named ports and Gateway API over Ingress, subPath for single-file overlays, anti-affinity and a PDB above one replica, stable SSA list keys, and GKE Inference Quickstart output used unfiltered for inference workloads.

inventory.description: Plans and configures multi-tenancy on GKE. Covers namespace isolation, RBAC planning for teams, resource quotas, LimitRanges, network isolation, and cost allocation. Use when designing GKE multi-tenancy, configuring GKE namespaces, setting up resource quotas, or isolating GKE teams. Don't use for single-tenant cluster configuration or general deployment instructions (use gke-basics or gke-app-onboarding instead).
inventory.goal: Set up a shared GKE cluster for several teams with namespace isolation, RBAC, quotas and network policy.
inventory.adds: Default to namespace-per-team and escalate isolation only when compliance requires it, bind RBAC to Google Groups through namespace Roles, pair every ResourceQuota with a LimitRange that sets default and defaultRequest whenever min or max is set, add a same-namespace-plus-DNS allow policy on top of default-deny, and label namespaces with cost-center for GKE cost allocation.

inventory.description: Plans, configures, and manages core GKE cluster networking. Covers private clusters, VPC-native configurations, DNS, node egress, Dataplane V2, and IP planning. Use when designing GKE networking layouts, configuring private clusters, setting up Dataplane V2, planning GKE IP ranges, or managing VPC- native cluster modes. Don't use for application ingress, load balancing, or service networking (use gke-service-networking instead).
inventory.goal: Set the network layout of a GKE cluster: private nodes, VPC-native ranges, Dataplane V2, DNS endpoint access, IP sizing and egress.
inventory.adds: Golden-path networking defaults for every cluster: private nodes with private-endpoint enforcement and DNS-endpoint access, Dataplane V2, Cloud DNS, intra-node visibility, auto IPAM with an auto-created subnet, and 48 max pods per node (110 only for high density), with VPC/subnet/ranges flagged as Day-0 decisions and Cloud NAT as the egress default.

inventory.description: Configures GKE observability, including Cloud Logging, Cloud Monitoring, and managed Prometheus. Use when configuring GKE monitoring, setting up GKE logging, or configuring Prometheus metrics collection. Don't use to configure local application logging frameworks or external APMs outside GKE.
inventory.goal: Configure logging, monitoring, managed Prometheus and alerts for a GKE cluster.
inventory.adds: Enable the golden-path component set including APISERVER, SCHEDULER and CONTROLLER_MANAGER metrics with managed Prometheus, name Cloud Monitoring as the alerting platform, always put API server latency on the dashboard, judge node health from node/status_condition together with instance_group/size, and use the listed alert thresholds.

inventory.description: Plans, configures, and hardens platform-level Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster security. Covers cluster add-ons (Secret Manager enablement), RBAC hardening (disabling insecure bindings, audit tools), Binary Authorization, Secrets Encryption (--database-encryption-key), Security Posture (--security-posture), enabling Shielded Nodes, GKE Sandbox cluster enablement, GKE IAM roles, and cross-service authentication IAM patterns. Use when securing cluster control planes, hardening GKE RBAC, enabling Shielded Nodes, enabling GKE Sandbox runtime, enabling cluster-wide security add-ons, or managing GKE IAM roles. Don't use for Workload Identity (use gke-workload-identity) or workload-level security (SecretProviderClass, PSS, NetPol, gVisor pod runtimeClassName; use gke-workload-security).
inventory.goal: Harden cluster-level GKE security: Secret Manager add-on, RBAC binding config, Binary Authorization, Shielded Nodes, GKE Sandbox enablement and IAM roles.
inventory.adds: Golden-path security defaults (Secret Manager add-on with 120s rotation, insecure system:authenticated and system:unauthenticated bindings disabled, secure boot and integrity monitoring, GKE_METADATA mode), a stance of starting IAM grants at container.viewer or container.developer, and a dedicated minimal node service account instead of the Compute Engine default.

inventory.description: Orchestrates comprehensive production readiness reviews and assessments for GKE clusters and workloads across scalability, security, reliability, observability, backup/DR, and cost optimization. Use when asked to productionize, prepare, assess, audit, or review a GKE cluster or workload before going live to production. Don't use for deep-dive single-domain implementation (use specific domain skills like gke-scaling, gke-platform-security, gke-workload-security, gke-service-networking, gke-reliability instead).
inventory.goal: Run a production-readiness review of a GKE cluster or workload by delegating each domain to its specialist skill and reporting a RAG score.
inventory.adds: The review is an orchestration, not an implementation: discover cluster and workload state first, invoke each domain skill in turn (onboarding, workload scaling, observability, reliability, platform and workload security, backup/DR, service networking, cost), then report a Red/Amber/Green status per area with an overall score and confirm with the user before any state-changing step.

inventory.description: Improves GKE workload reliability, using PDBs, health probes, and topology spread constraints. Use when configuring GKE workload reliability, setting up PDBs, or configuring GKE health probes (liveness, readiness, startup). Don't use for disaster recovery setup or full cluster backups (use gke-backup-dr instead).
inventory.goal: Make GKE workloads survive node, zone and upgrade disruptions with PDBs, health probes, graceful shutdown and topology spread.
inventory.adds: House defaults: regional four-zone cluster on the REGULAR channel with SURGE upgrades and auto-repair/upgrade; a PDB on every production workload with 2+ replicas; liveness and readiness probes on every container with explicit initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds and timeoutSeconds; a preStop sleep for load-balancer deregistration; hard zone spread plus soft node spread; and a minimum-replica table per workload type (2 stateless, 3 critical or stateful, 1 batch).

inventory.description: Configures GKE edge networking, traffic routing, load balancing, and private service endpoints. Use when configuring Gateway API manifests, standard Ingress, Cloud Armor WAF security policies, Container-Native Load Balancing (NEGs), Private Service Connect (PSC), or Google-managed SSL certificates on GKE. Don't use for core cluster IP planning, Dataplane V2 network policies, or node NAT egress (use gke-networking instead).
inventory.goal: Expose GKE services to the internet or other VPCs with Gateway API or Ingress, Cloud Armor, managed certificates, NEGs and Private Service Connect.
inventory.adds: Prefer Gateway API (gatewayClass gke-l7-global-external-managed) over Ingress, always front public endpoints with Cloud Armor, use Google-managed certificates, and always use container-native load balancing (NEGs) for HTTP(S).

inventory.description: Manages GKE storage, including PVCs, PersistentVolumes, Filestore, and GCS FUSE. Use when configuring GKE storage, creating PVCs, or setting up GCS FUSE on GKE. Don't use for database administration or replication strategies outside volume provisioning context.
inventory.goal: Provision and resize persistent storage for GKE workloads with the right StorageClass, Filestore for shared access and GCS FUSE for bucket mounts.
inventory.adds: Golden-path CSI set (PD, Filestore, GCS FUSE, Parallelstore; pd-balanced boot disks) and StorageClass defaults: allowVolumeExpansion true on every class, regional-pd and WaitForFirstConsumer for production, pd-ssd for databases and pd-balanced otherwise, Filestore for RWX, GCS FUSE for data pipelines, MCP patch_k8s_resource preferred over kubectl, and PVC backup through gke-backup-dr.

inventory.description: Monitors, troubleshoots, and manages GKE TPU Dynamic Slices custom resources. Use when checking TPU slice lifecycle states, troubleshooting slice provisioning failures, validating single-slice or multi-slice (JobSet) workload manifests, or safely patching stuck finalizers and disabling the slice controller. Don't use for generic GKE cluster node pool creation or standard non-TPU workload management (use gke-basics or gke-cluster-creation instead).
inventory.goal: Inspect GKE TPU Dynamic Slice custom resources, explain their lifecycle state, check workload manifests target a slice correctly, and clean up stuck slices or the slice controller safely.
inventory.adds: Start every slice question with kubectl describe slice and read Status.Conditions against the fixed state/reason table and the three-point provisioning checklist; never remove a slice finalizer or disable the slice controller without quoting the exact command and getting explicit user confirmation.

inventory.description: Monitors and troubleshoots GKE TPU workloads, nodes, and node pools using GKE system metrics and PromQL. Use when monitoring TensorCore duty cycle, TPU memory, node readiness, multi-host TPU node pool availability, host maintenance or preemption interruptions, and calculating MTTR or MTBI metrics for GKE TPUs. Don't use for general non-TPU GKE workload monitoring or non-metric TPU debugging.
inventory.goal: Tell whether a GKE TPU workload's interruptions or slowness come from the nodes and node pools underneath it, using GKE system metrics and ready-made PromQL.
inventory.adds: A fixed diagnostic order (confirm metric export on port 8431, runtime duty cycle and memory, node Ready condition, node-pool status and multi-host availability, interruption counts by type/reason, then 7-day MTTR and MTBI) with the exact PromQL for each, and a threshold of duty cycle under 20% during training as underutilization.

inventory.description: Plans, executes, and validates Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster upgrades and maintenance operations for both Standard and Autopilot clusters. Produces upgrade plans, pre/post-upgrade checklists, maintenance runbooks with gcloud commands, release channel strategy, and troubleshooting guides. Handles node pool upgrade strategies (surge, blue-green), version compatibility, PDB management, and workload-specific concerns (stateful, GPU, operators). Use this skill whenever the user mentions GKE upgrades, Kubernetes version bumps, node pool maintenance, GKE patching, cluster version management, release channel selection, maintenance windows, surge upgrades, stuck upgrades, or any GKE lifecycle management task — even casual mentions like "we need to upgrade our clusters" or "plan our next GKE maintenance" or "our upgrade is stuck." Don't use for GKE cluster creation, application onboarding, general networking/routing setup, or security policy configurations (use gke-basics or relevant GKE skills instead).
inventory.goal: Plan, run and troubleshoot GKE control-plane and node-pool upgrades, producing plans, checklists and runbooks tailored to the cluster.

inventory.description: Configures and diagnoses Workload Identity Federation for GKE authentication failures for Pods (403 "iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken" / permission denied, "could not find default credentials", or GKE metadata server unreachable) by verifying cluster and node-pool Workload Identity configuration, the Kubernetes ServiceAccount (KSA) to IAM binding (direct principal binding and legacy Google ServiceAccount impersonation), target-resource IAM roles, and gke-metadata-server health.
